measured.contract: keeps every bone, animation, attachment and bodypart of the base

M1.reason: The measured overlap clears the line in every view (0.835 front/back, 0.82 left/right, 0.838 top/below), but there are visible outline faults the measurement does not penalise. A bulky raised pad on one shoulder sticks up above the original's sloped shoulder line. It is clearest in the back, back-left and front views, on the figure's left shoulder. The boots end in square, box-like blocks with flat toes and heels that stick out in the left, right, front-left and back-left views, where the original has shaped, rounded boots. Width is also 6.9% over the original (offShare 0.069).

M2.reason: Measured 25.3 x 22.2 x 69.2 against 23.7 x 22.0 x 69.4. Width is 6.8% over, the other two are within 1%, so all three are inside 10%.

M3.reason: The balaclava, short-sleeved black shirt, vest, tattooed bare forearms, fingerless gloves, belt, camo trousers, thigh pouch, knee pads and tall boots are all there and in place. Two are the wrong shape. The boots are blocky boxes with square toes instead of the original's laced, round-toed boots (left/right and front-left views). The vest has an extra raised, lumpy pad over one shoulder that the original does not have (back and back-left views), which makes the shoulders look uneven.

M4.reason: The measured mean is 3.1 (worst view 3.7, below), far under 15. Each region keeps the original's colour and material: a black cloth mask and shirt, a black vest, grey-white urban camo trousers, tan skin on the arms and black leather boots. The skin reads slightly darker and redder, but it is the same colour.

M5.reason: The markings are there in their places but softer. The gold '511' on the back reads smeared, close to '5H1' (back and back-left views). The row of gold cartridges and the chest lettering on the vest front are muddy and hard to read compared with the original's crisp ones (front and front-right views). The tattoos and camo pattern are present but blurrier. The boot lacing detail is mostly lost on the boxy boots.

M6.reason: At game size it reads as the same masked merc in a black vest and grey camo, so the overall impression is close. A player would still notice the square block feet in profile and the lumpy, uneven shoulder, and the vest's front lettering is muddier. It is near the original but would not pass a side-by-side as the same model.

M7.reason: It faces the same way as the original, stands upright in the same idle pose, and its feet sit at the same height on the origin as the original's in every view.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. It has 1296 triangles against the original's 873, under the 1746 limit. No open, inside-out or floating parts are visible in any view.

C1.reason: Through the run, every part stays attached and follows the limbs in the same phases as the original, with nothing sinking or floating. Through the forward dive, the body stays whole from the leap to lying flat with arms forward. The dive's timing differs (35 frames against the original's 22, and the opening crouch is shorter). That comes from the base skeleton's animation, which the contract requires it to keep, not from a part failing. A light patch at the crotch in run frames 17 and 21 looks like the camo texture, not a tear.

C2.reason: Measured by compareContract: it keeps every bone, animation, attachment and bodypart of the base, with no faults reported.
